Chaïm Soutine was born into a poor Jewish family in a small village in what is now Belarus. He moved to Paris in 1913, where he lived and painted in a crowded artists' colony and became close friends with Modigliani. His wild, twisting paintings of waiters, pastry cooks and landscapes made him famous. He died in Paris in 1943, during the German occupation.

Eduard Bendemann was born in Berlin to a Jewish family and became one of Germany's leading painters. He studied in Berlin and then worked in Dresden and Düsseldorf, where he became the director of the art academy. His paintings of Bible stories and everyday life were admired all over Europe. He died in Düsseldorf in 1889.

Ephraim Moses Lilien was born in Drohobych, in the region of Galicia, then part of Austria, and grew up in a Jewish family. He studied art in Kraków and Munich, and later lived in Berlin. He was an early artist of the Zionist movement and illustrated books with beautiful Art Nouveau designs. He died in Germany in 1925.

Isaac Israëls was born in Amsterdam, the son of the famous painter Jozef Israëls, in a Dutch Jewish family. He painted lively scenes of Amsterdam streets, fashion houses and beaches in a loose, fast Impressionist style. He lived in Amsterdam, Paris, and The Hague, and he traveled to Indonesia and elsewhere. He died in The Hague in 1934.

Isidor Kaufmann was born in Arad, then part of Hungary, to a Jewish family and trained in Vienna. He is best known for his warm, realistic portraits of Jewish people and religious scenes in Eastern Europe. He lived and worked in Vienna for much of his life. He died there in 1921.

Issachar Ber Ryback was born in Ukraine, then part of the Russian Empire, to a Jewish family. He studied art in Kyiv and was part of a group that tried to create a modern Jewish art. In 1926 he moved to Paris, where he stayed until his death in 1935. He painted and drew Jewish village life.

Jozef Israëls was born into a Jewish family in Groningen, in the Netherlands, and became the leader of the Hague School of painters. He is famous for his tender pictures of fisherfolk and poor families in the dunes. He lived in Amsterdam and The Hague, and spent many summers in the fishing village of Zandvoort. He died in 1911.

Léon Bakst was born in Grodno, then part of the Russian Empire, to a Jewish family. He became a star of the Ballets Russes in Paris, designing the vivid costumes and sets that astonished audiences. He also painted portraits and illustrated books. He died in France in 1924.

Mark Gertler was born in London to Jewish immigrants from Poland and grew up in the poor neighborhood of Spitalfields. He studied at the Slade School of Art and became a friend of many writers and artists of his time. He is best known for his bold, rounded paintings, such as 'Merry-Go-Round'. He died in London in 1939.

Maurycy Gottlieb was born in Drohobych, in Galicia, to a Jewish family and studied art in Kraków, Vienna and Munich. He was a student of the great painter Jan Matejko and painted striking pictures of Jewish life and history. He died in Kraków in 1879 at only 22. His few works are treasured today.

Max Liebermann was born in Berlin to a wealthy Jewish family and became the leading German Impressionist. He painted workers, beer gardens and gardens, and he served as president of the Prussian Academy of Arts. After the Nazis came to power in 1933, he was forced to give up his positions. He died in Berlin in 1935.

Moritz Daniel Oppenheim was born in Hanau, Germany, to a Jewish family and trained in Munich, Paris and Rome. He lived mostly in Frankfurt, where he became a favorite painter of the Rothschild family. He is best known for warm pictures of traditional Jewish family life. He died in Frankfurt in 1882.

Samuel Hirszenberg was born in Łódź, Poland, to a Jewish family and studied in Kraków, Munich and Paris. His large paintings show the suffering and hopes of Jewish people in Eastern Europe. In 1907 he moved to Jerusalem to teach at the new Bezalel art school. He died there the next year.

Solomon Alexander Hart was born in Plymouth, England, to a Jewish family and trained in London. In 1840 he became the first Jewish member of the Royal Academy. He painted history scenes, portraits and pictures of Jewish life. He died in London in 1881.

Yosef Zvi Geiger was a painter from Safed, in the Holy Land under Ottoman rule. He painted religious scenes and local life in a simple, heartfelt style. He lived and worked in Safed, a town famous for Jewish study. He is remembered as one of the earliest painters from the land of Israel.

Aaron Allan Edson was born in Quebec and became a Canadian landscape painter who painted the forests and mountains of the east. He lived in Montreal and worked in Quebec and New England. His quiet, glowing landscapes were very popular. He died in 1888.

Antoine Plamondon was born near Quebec City and studied painting in Paris in the 1830s. He became one of the most important portrait painters in Quebec, painting priests, nuns and political leaders. He taught many younger artists. He died in 1895.

Charles Alexander Smith was a Canadian painter born in Galt, Ontario, in 1864. He painted historical scenes and portraits. He later lived in London, England, where he died in 1915. His painting of the 'Assembly of the Six Counties' recorded an important event in Quebec history.

Charles Huot was born in Quebec City and studied painting in Paris. He became one of Quebec's most important history painters, creating large murals for the Quebec Legislature. He also taught drawing and illustrated books. He died in 1930.

Clarence Gagnon was born in Montreal and studied in Paris. He is best known for his bright, colorful paintings of Quebec villages in winter, and also for illustrating the novel 'Maria Chapdelaine'. He lived part of his life in France and part in Quebec. He died in Montreal in 1942.

Cornelius Krieghoff was born in Amsterdam and moved to North America as a young man. He lived in Montreal and Quebec, where he painted lively scenes of French-Canadian farm life and winter. His humorous pictures made him one of Canada's most popular painters. He died in Chicago in 1872.

David Milne was born in Ontario and lived in New York, then returned to the Ontario woods in 1930. He painted with a delicate touch, using watercolors and thin oils to capture cities, flowers and woods. He is considered one of Canada's greatest modern painters. He died in 1953.

Emily Carr was born in Victoria, British Columbia, and studied art in San Francisco, London and France. She became famous for her paintings of the forests, totem poles and Indigenous villages of the Pacific coast. She was also a writer and lived with many pets. She died in Victoria in 1945.

Eugène Hamel was born in Quebec City and became a Canadian painter and a portrait artist. He painted people of Wendake and other communities, as well as religious paintings. He lived most of his life in Quebec. He died in 1932.

Frederick Arthur Verner was born in Ontario and became famous for paintings of the Canadian plains, with buffalo and Indigenous camps at sunset. He spent his later years in England, where he continued to paint Canadian scenes. He died in London in 1928.

George Agnew Reid was born in Ontario and trained in Philadelphia and Paris. He was a leading Toronto painter, a teacher, and the president of the Ontario College of Art. During World War I he painted Canadian factory workers and street scenes. He died in 1947.
Henri Beau was born in Montreal and studied in Paris, where he spent much of his life. He painted historical scenes of Canada and later official war paintings. He died in Paris in 1949.

Henry Sandham was born in Montreal and became a leading Canadian painter, illustrator and a founding member of the Royal Canadian Academy. He later lived in Boston and London. His landscapes and harbor scenes were widely admired. He died in London in 1910.

Homer Watson was born in Doon, Ontario, near what is now Kitchener, and taught himself to paint. He became known for his dramatic pictures of fields, skies and rivers, and was admired by Oscar Wilde. He is considered a pioneer of Canadian landscape painting. He died in Kitchener in 1936.

Horatio Walker was born in Listowel, Ontario, and became a famous painter of rural Quebec. He lived much of the year on Île d'Orléans near Quebec City and painted farmers and animals in a soft, glowing light. His paintings sold well in the United States. He died in Quebec in 1938.

William Brymner was born in Scotland and raised in Canada. He studied in Paris and became an influential teacher at the Art Association of Montreal, where he taught many of the country's best-known painters. His own paintings show women and children in warm, soft light. He died in 1925.

James Wilson Morrice was born in Montreal and spent most of his life in Paris, where he became a friend of Matisse. He painted quiet landscapes and city scenes in bright, simple colors, and also traveled to North Africa and the Caribbean. He is regarded as Canada's first modern painter. He died in Tunis in 1924.

Joseph Légaré was born in Quebec City and was one of the first painters in Canada to paint landscapes and historical events. He collected European paintings and taught himself by copying them. He was also a politician and a businessman. He died in 1855.

Laura Muntz Lyall was born in England and raised in Canada. She studied in Toronto and in Paris and became known for gentle, soft pictures of mothers and children. She was one of the leading women painters of her time. She died in Toronto in 1930.

Lawren Harris was born in Brantford, Ontario, and was a founding member of the Group of Seven. He became known for his bold, simple paintings of Lake Superior, the Rocky Mountains and the Arctic. His work shaped the idea of the Canadian landscape. He died in Vancouver in 1970.

Marc-Aurèle de Foy Suzor-Coté was born in Arthabaska, Quebec, and studied in Paris. He painted both traditional pictures and bright landscapes of the snowy Quebec countryside. He also made sculptures. He died in Florida in 1937.

Maurice Cullen was born in St. John's, Newfoundland, and grew up in Montreal. He studied in Paris, and became known for his glowing paintings of snowy Montreal and the St. Lawrence River. In World War I he served as an official Canadian war artist. He died in 1934.

Paul Kane was born in Ireland and grew up in Toronto. Between 1845 and 1848 he made a long journey across Canada to the Pacific, sketching Indigenous peoples and landscapes. He then painted a series of large pictures from his sketches. He died in Toronto in 1871.

Paul Peel was born in London, Ontario, and studied in Philadelphia and in Paris, where he became a successful painter. His warm, sunny pictures of children won prizes at the Paris Salon. He died young, in Paris, at the age of 31.

Robert Harris was born in Wales and raised in Prince Edward Island. He studied in London and Paris and became one of Canada's leading portrait painters, and the president of the Royal Canadian Academy. He is best known for his painting of the Fathers of Confederation. He died in Montreal in 1919.

Théophile Hamel was born near Quebec City and studied in Europe in the 1840s. He became one of the most important portrait painters in Canada, painting political leaders and church figures. He lived in Quebec City. He died there in 1870.

Tom Thomson was born in Ontario and worked as a commercial artist in Toronto before devoting himself to painting. He spent his summers in Algonquin Park, making small colorful oil sketches of lakes, trees and skies. His friends who later formed the Group of Seven were inspired by him. He drowned in Canoe Lake in 1917, and his death is still a famous mystery.

William Blair Bruce was born in Hamilton, Ontario, and lived in Europe for most of his career, in France and Sweden. He painted landscapes and dramatic scenes. His paintings and sculptures are now in a museum he planned in his hometown. He died in Stockholm in 1906.

William Raphael was born in Poland, then part of Prussia, and moved to Montreal as a young man. He painted the streets, markets and views of Montreal and Quebec in the 1860s. His pictures record the city as it was. He died in Montreal in 1914.

Zacharie Vincent was a Huron-Wendat painter from Wendake, near Quebec City. He is considered the first Indigenous painter in Quebec, and he often signed his portraits 'Zacharie Vincent Telariolin, the last of the Hurons'. He painted himself and his family in traditional dress. He died in 1886.

Asta Nørregaard was born in Christiania (now Oslo) and was one of Norway's first professional women painters. She studied in Munich and Paris and painted portraits, including one of Edvard Munch. She was an important supporter of other artists. She died in 1933.

Fredrik Kolstø was a Norwegian painter born in 1860 in the region of Haugesund and studied in Paris. He painted historical and landscape pictures. He lived in Trondheim for part of his life. He died in 1945.

Hans Heyerdahl was born in Norway, to a family of Norwegian-Swedish roots, and studied in Copenhagen, Munich and Paris. He painted portraits and religious paintings with a clear, quiet realism. He became one of the leading Norwegian painters of his generation. He died in Oslo in 1913.

Christian Krohg was born near Christiania (now Oslo) and was a painter, writer and a leader of the Realist movement in Norway. He studied in Germany and France and painted fishermen, poor people and the sea. He supported social change and caused controversy with his novel and paintings. He died in Oslo in 1925.

Otto Sinding was a Norwegian painter born in Kongsberg in 1842, who studied in Munich. He painted dramatic mountain landscapes and scenes of folk life. He lived in Munich and in Norway. He died in 1909.
Amaldus Nielsen was a Norwegian landscape painter who painted the wild mountains and fjords of Norway. He studied in Düsseldorf and Munich. He lived to the age of 94 and died in Oslo in 1932.

Gerhard Munthe was a Norwegian painter and designer, born in 1849. He was a leader in reviving Norwegian folk art and illustrated Norse sagas. His bright, decorative style influenced Norwegian design. He died in Lysaker in 1929.

Eilif Peterssen was born in Christiania and studied in Munich, Paris and Italy. He painted historical scenes, portraits and landscapes, and helped bring the Realist style to Norway. He lived in Oslo and in Lysaker. He died in 1928.

Thorolf Holmboe was a Norwegian painter born in 1866 who painted landscapes and winter scenes. He studied in Norway and in Paris. He lived most of his life in and around Christiania (now Oslo). He died in 1935.

Christian Skredsvig was a Norwegian painter and writer born in Modum in 1854, who studied in Paris and lived in Eggedal. His paintings show Norwegian farm life and rural people in soft light. He also wrote stories and novels. He died in 1924.
Gustav Lærum was a Norwegian painter born in 1870, who painted portraits and landscapes. He studied in Norway and Paris. He worked in Oslo. He died in 1938.
Carl Sundt-Hansen was born in Stavanger, Norway, in 1841, and spent much of his life in Denmark. He painted scenes of Norwegian and Danish peasant life. He died in Stavanger in 1907.
Axel Ender was a Norwegian painter born in 1853 in Asker. He studied in Germany and painted landscapes and folk scenes. He lived in Christiania (Oslo). He died in 1920.
Severin Segelcke was a Norwegian painter born in Christiania in 1867. He painted landscapes and portraits and lived part of his life in Norway's countryside. He died in 1940.
Jacob Bratland was a Norwegian painter born in Bergen in 1859. He studied in Germany and painted landscapes of western Norway. He died in Christiania in 1906.
Karl Uchermann was a Norwegian painter born in the Lofoten region in 1855. He painted scenes of Northern Norway and of animals, particularly dogs. He lived in Oslo. He died in 1940.
Elisabeth Sinding was a Norwegian painter born in 1846, and one of the earlier women painters in her country. She painted landscapes and portraits. She lived in Oslo until her death in 1930.

Carl Frithjof Smith was born in Christiania (Oslo) in 1859 and trained in Germany, where he lived in Weimar for much of his life. He painted quiet scenes of family life and portraits. He died in Weimar in 1917.

Erik Werenskiold was born in Kongsvinger, Norway, and was one of the leading Norwegian painters of his generation. He is famous for his realistic scenes of Norwegian life and for illustrating Norwegian folk tales with Theodor Kittelsen. He also painted portraits of famous Norwegians. He died in Oslo in 1938.
Fredrik Borgen was a Norwegian landscape painter born in 1852, known for paintings of winter scenes and evening light. He studied in Germany. He died in Christiania in 1907.

Frits Thaulow was born in Christiania (Oslo) and became a leading Norwegian Impressionist, known for painting water in rivers, streams and mills. He lived in France and Denmark, as well as in Norway. He died in 1906.
Gunnar Berg was a Norwegian painter born in 1863 in the Lofoten region, known for his scenes of fjords and northern Norway. He studied in Germany. He died young, at 29, in Berlin in 1893.

Gustav Wentzel was born in Christiania in 1859 and became a Norwegian painter of everyday scenes and portraits. He studied in Paris and Munich and lived later in Lillehammer. His honest interiors were praised. He died in 1927.

Halfdan Egedius was born in Drammen in 1877 and became one of the most promising Norwegian painters of his generation, especially for his landscapes and book illustrations. He died of illness at the age of 22, in 1899.

Ole Peter Hansen Balling was born in Christiania and moved to the United States in 1856. He fought in the American Civil War and painted portraits of President Lincoln, Ulysses S. Grant and other leaders. He later returned to Norway. He died in 1906.

Harriet Backer was born in Holmestrand, Norway, and became one of the country's greatest painters. She studied in Munich and Paris and became famous for her glowing pictures of rooms and churches. She also ran a painting school that trained many young artists. She died in Oslo in 1932.
Joachim Frich was a Norwegian landscape painter born in Bergen in 1810. He studied in Dresden with Johan Christian Dahl. He painted the fjords and mountains of Norway. He died in Christiania in 1858.

Kitty Kielland was born in Stavanger, Norway, and was one of the first Norwegian women to become a leading landscape painter. She lived in Germany and France for many years. Her atmospheric pictures of Norwegian summer light are admired today. She died in 1914.

Lars Hertervig was born on an island near Stavanger, Norway, and studied in Düsseldorf. He struggled with mental illness, was often poor, and was little understood in his lifetime. His glowing, dreamy landscapes are now seen as among the finest in Norwegian art. He died in Stavanger in 1902.
Ludvig Karsten was a Norwegian painter born in Christiania in 1876. He lived a free, bohemian life, traveling in Europe and painting in bold, bright colors. He died in Paris in 1926.
Martin Borgord was born in Gausdal, Norway, in 1869, and became a painter of history and portraits. He studied in Germany and spent time in the United States. He died in 1935.

Oda Krohg was born in Oslo and was a painter who became a leading figure of the Norwegian bohemian circle. She studied in Paris and Germany. She was married to the painter Christian Krohg. She died in Oslo in 1935.

Oscar Wergeland was born in Christiania in 1844 and became a Norwegian painter of history. His huge painting of the Norwegian constitution of 1814 is one of Norway's best-known pictures. He died in 1910.

Peter Nicolai Arbo was a Norwegian painter born in 1831 who studied in Düsseldorf and Munich. He painted Norse myth and Viking history, making them familiar to Norwegians. His 'Wild Hunt of Odin' is his most famous painting. He died in Christiania in 1892.
Ragnhild Keyser was a Norwegian painter born in Oslo in 1889, who studied in Norway and Paris. She painted still lifes and landscapes with a quiet, careful style. She died in Oslo in 1943.

Thomas Fearnley was born in Halden, Norway, in 1802 and studied in Copenhagen and Stockholm. He traveled widely in Europe and was a friend of J. C. Dahl and J. M. W. Turner. He painted landscapes in Italy, Switzerland and Norway. He died young in Munich in 1842.

Asher Brown Durand was born in New Jersey and began as an engraver before becoming a landscape painter. He was a leader of the Hudson River School and the second president of the National Academy of Design. His painting 'Kindred Spirits' is a famous American image. He died in 1886.

Charles Willson Peale was born in Maryland and became one of the best-known American painters of the Revolution. He painted George Washington many times, fought in the war, and also founded a museum in Philadelphia. He lived in Philadelphia and died there in 1827.

Childe Hassam was born near Boston and became a leading American Impressionist. He painted the streets and parks of New York, and a famous series of flag paintings. He also painted on the coast of Maine and at Appledore Island. He died in East Hampton, New York, in 1935.

Edmund Charles Tarbell was born in Massachusetts and was a leading Boston painter. He taught at the Museum School in Boston and painted graceful pictures of women in sunlit rooms. He later lived in New Hampshire. He died in 1938.

George Bellows was born in Columbus, Ohio, and moved to New York City, where he became a leading painter of city life. He painted boxing matches, tenements and the construction of Penn Station. He died young, in 1925, at 42.

George Caleb Bingham was born in Virginia and raised in Missouri. He painted the life of the Missouri and Mississippi rivers, from flatboatmen to election days. He also served in Missouri politics. He died in Kansas City in 1879.

George Catlin was born in Pennsylvania and trained as a lawyer before becoming a painter. In the 1830s he traveled across the American West to paint portraits of Native Americans and their lives. He hoped to preserve a record of cultures he feared would disappear. He died in New Jersey in 1872.

John Gast was a painter and lithographer born in Berlin, Germany, who worked in Brooklyn, New York. He is known for his 1872 painting 'American Progress', which became a symbol of westward expansion. He died in Brooklyn in 1896.

John Quidor was born in New Jersey and worked in New York City. He made humorous, wild illustrations of stories by Washington Irving, such as 'Rip Van Winkle' and 'Sleepy Hollow'. He was not widely known in his lifetime. He died in Jersey City in 1881.

John Rose was a painter in the late 1700s who lived in the Colony of South Carolina. His watercolor 'The Old Plantation' is one of the earliest paintings to show the lives of enslaved African Americans. Little else is known about him.

John Vanderlyn was born in Kingston, New York, and studied art in Paris. He was one of the first American painters to be trained in Europe, and painted large panoramas and history pictures. He painted 'Landing of Columbus' for the U.S. Capitol. He died in Kingston in 1852.

Martin Johnson Heade was born in Pennsylvania and traveled widely. He is famous for his misty salt marshes, stormy skies, and his paintings of hummingbirds and orchids in Brazil. He settled in Florida late in life. He died in St. Augustine in 1904.

Richard Edward Miller was born in St. Louis, Missouri, and studied in Paris. He joined the American art colony at Giverny, near Monet's home, and painted bright Impressionist scenes of women in sunlit rooms. He later lived in Provincetown, Massachusetts. He died in 1943.

Thomas Pollock Anshutz was a painter and teacher born in Kentucky and active in Philadelphia. He taught at the Pennsylvania Academy of the Fine Arts, where his students included Robert Henri and Charles Demuth. He died in 1912.

Winslow Homer was born in Boston and became one of America's greatest painters. He started as an illustrator and covered the Civil War for a magazine. Later, he lived on the rocky coast of Maine, where he painted the sea, fishermen and storms. He died at his home at Prouts Neck in 1910.

Fujishima Takeji was born in Kagoshima, Japan, and became one of the first Japanese painters to master Western oil painting. He studied in Paris and Rome. He later taught art in Tokyo. He died in Tokyo in 1943.

Harada Naojirō was born in Edo (now Tokyo) and studied painting in Germany. He was one of the first Japanese artists to learn Western oil painting abroad, and he painted some of Japan's early oil paintings. He died in 1899.

Itō Jakuchū was born in Kyoto, Japan, the son of a vegetable seller. He ran the family shop for years before devoting himself to painting, and kept chickens in his garden so he could study them. His colorful and detailed pictures of birds, plants and animals are among the most beloved in Japan. He died in 1800.

Kanō Eigaku was a Japanese painter of the Kanō school, a family of artists that painted for Japan's rulers for hundreds of years. He worked in the late Edo and Meiji periods. He was famous for traditional pictures of Japanese life. He died in 1867.

Katsushika Hokusai was born in Edo (now Tokyo) and worked as an artist for over 70 years. He made thousands of drawings and woodblock prints, including The Great Wave and the Thirty-Six Views of Mount Fuji. He changed his name dozens of times and said he hoped to get better until he was 110. He died in 1849, at about age 89.

Kawamura Kiyoo was a Japanese painter born in Edo in 1852. He studied Western-style painting in Italy and helped bring oil painting to Japan. He painted historical scenes and legends. He died in 1934.

Konishi Hirosada was a Japanese printmaker who lived in Osaka from about 1810 to 1864. He is known for woodblock prints of kabuki actors. His prints were collected by fans like trading cards. He lived in the city's theater district.

Maruyama Ōkyo was born into a farming family near Kyoto and became one of the most important Japanese painters of the 1700s. He taught himself to paint from nature and was famous for his realistic animals and plants. He founded the Maruyama school. He died in Kyoto in 1795.

Ogata Kenzan was born in Kyoto and was a famous potter and painter. He was the younger brother of the painter Ogata Kōrin, and together they made some of the most beautiful objects of their time. He decorated ceramics with simple, beautiful designs. He died in Edo (Tokyo) in 1743.

Ogata Kōrin was born in Kyoto into a rich family of fabric merchants and became one of Japan's greatest decorative painters. He founded the Rinpa style of bold shapes and gold leaf. His folding screens, such as 'Red and White Plum Blossoms', are national treasures. He died in Kyoto in 1716.

Ryūsai Shigeharu was a Japanese printmaker who worked in Osaka in the early 1800s. He made woodblock prints of kabuki actors and scenes of the theater. Fans bought these prints to remember their favorite performers.

Sakai Hōitsu was born in Edo (Tokyo) to a samurai family and became a leading painter of the Rinpa school. He admired Ogata Kōrin and worked to revive his style. He painted flowers, birds and the seasons. He died in 1828.

Uemura Shōen was born in Kyoto, and became one of Japan's greatest women painters. She was best known for beautiful pictures of women in traditional style. She was the first woman to receive the Order of Culture, Japan's high honor, in 1948. She died in 1949.

Suzuki Kiitsu was born in Edo (Tokyo) and studied under Sakai Hōitsu. He painted flowers, plants and scenes of nature in the Rinpa style, with bold colors and graceful shapes. He is admired for his modern-looking designs. He died in 1858.

Takeuchi Seihō was born in Kyoto and became one of the leading painters of Japan in the early 1900s. He studied Western painting during trips to Europe and mixed it with Japanese styles. He is known for animals, such as his famous 'Tabby Cat'. He died in 1942.

Utagawa Hiroshige was born in Edo (Tokyo) and became one of Japan's greatest print artists. He is known for his landscapes, such as the Fifty-three Stations of the Tōkaidō and One Hundred Famous Views of Edo. Van Gogh and Monet admired his work. He died in 1858.

The Kangxi Emperor was the second Qing emperor of China, and he ruled for 61 years, from 1661 to 1722, longer than any other Chinese emperor. He was interested in science, art, poetry and calligraphy, and also painted himself. He lived in Beijing and the Imperial Summer Palace.

Xu Yang was a court painter in China in the 1700s, born in Suzhou. He painted big, detailed scrolls recording life in the city and the Qianlong Emperor's travels. His pictures are treasured as history. He lived and worked in the Qing court.

Abdülmecid II was born in Istanbul in 1868 and was the last caliph of the Ottoman family. He was also a talented painter and music lover. After Turkey became a republic, he was forced into exile. He died in Paris in 1944.

Kamal-ol-Molk was born in Kashan, Iran, in 1848 and became the court painter of the Qajar kings. He studied European painting and painted portraits and scenes of daily life with great realism. He later founded an art school in Tehran. He died in Nishapur in 1940.

Agustín Arrieta was born in Chiautempan and worked in Puebla, Mexico. He painted still lifes and kitchen scenes with great skill, as well as portraits. His paintings show details of everyday Mexican life. He died in 1874.

Guadalupe Carpio was a Mexican painter born in Xalapa in 1828, and one of the first women to study at the Academy of San Carlos in Mexico City. She painted portraits and scenes of daily life. She died in 1892.

José María Obregón was born in Mexico City and studied at the Academy of San Carlos. He painted historical scenes, including 'The Discovery of Pulque', and was a leading artist in his country. He died in 1902.

José María Jara was a Mexican painter born in 1866 who studied at the Academy of San Carlos in Mexico City. He painted scenes of Mexican life, with a special interest in customs and traditions. He died in 1939.

José María Velasco was born in a village in Mexico and became the country's most famous landscape painter. He was also a scientist who studied plants, animals and the sky. His paintings of the Valley of Mexico show its volcanoes and lakes. He died in Mexico City in 1912.

Manuel Ocaranza was born in Uruapan, Mexico, in 1841 and studied at the Academy of San Carlos in Mexico City. He painted romantic scenes and portraits and was one of the best Mexican painters of his time. He died young, at 41, in 1882.

Saturnino Herrán was born in Aguascalientes, Mexico, in 1887, and moved to Mexico City to study art. He painted Mexican workers, Indigenous people and traditions in a bold, strong style. He helped inspire later Mexican muralists. He died in 1918 at only 31.

Ángel Zárraga was born in Durango, Mexico, and lived in Paris for many years. He mixed Mexican themes with the modern styles of Europe, including Cubism. He painted large murals as well as portraits. He died in Mexico in 1946.

Anders Zorn was born in the Swedish region of Dalarna and became one of the most famous painters of his time. He was a master of watercolor and painted portraits of presidents, including Theodore Roosevelt. He made a home in Mora, Sweden, where his house is now a museum. He died in 1920.
Carl Gustaf Hellqvist was born in Sweden in 1851 and studied in Stockholm and Munich. He painted large history paintings full of drama. He died young, in Munich, at 39.

Carl Gustaf Pilo was born in Sweden in 1711 and worked for many years as a court painter in Denmark before moving to Stockholm. He painted portraits of royalty, and started a large painting of the coronation of King Gustav III. He died in 1793.

Carl Larsson was born in Stockholm to a poor family and became one of Sweden's best-loved painters. He is famous for his watercolors of his own home and family in Sundborn, which show happy children, flowers and sunshine. He also painted large murals. He died in 1919.

Gustaf Cederström was born in Stockholm in 1845 and was a Swedish painter known for dramatic history paintings. He studied in Düsseldorf and Paris. He later became director of the Royal Academy of Fine Arts. He died in 1933.

Hanna Hirsch-Pauli was born in Stockholm in 1864 and was a leading Swedish woman painter. She studied in Stockholm and Paris and was a friend of many Nordic painters. She is best known for her warm family scenes. She died in 1940.
Mårten Eskil Winge was born in Stockholm and became a leading Swedish history painter. He studied in Düsseldorf and Paris and painted subjects from Norse mythology. He died in Enköping in 1896.
Oscar Björck was born in Stockholm in 1860 and was a Swedish painter and teacher. He spent time in the Skagen artists' colony in Denmark. He painted portraits and landscapes. He died in 1929.
Richard Bergh was born in Stockholm in 1858 and became one of Sweden's leading painters of the 'Nordic light'. He was also a director of the National Museum. He died in 1919.

Eero Järnefelt was born in Vyborg and became a leading Finnish painter of rural life and landscapes. He studied in Saint Petersburg and Paris. His family included the composer Jean Sibelius, who was his brother-in-law. He died in Helsinki in 1937.

Werner Holmberg was a Finnish landscape painter born in Helsinki in 1830. He studied in Düsseldorf in Germany, where he died of illness at only 30. His paintings of Finnish forests and fields were important for Finnish art.

Christen Købke was born in Copenhagen and was a leading painter of the Danish Golden Age. He painted views of the city, the shore and portraits of friends with a light, delicate touch. He died in 1848, at 37.

Johan Thomas Lundbye was a Danish painter born in Kalundborg in 1818. He painted fields, animals and old monuments of the Danish countryside. He died young, at 29, in 1848, during the first Schleswig War.

Vilhelm Hammershøi was born in Copenhagen and became famous for his quiet, gray pictures of empty rooms and of his wife Ida. His soft colors and calm mood are unforgettable. He lived and worked in Copenhagen all his life. He died in 1916.

Henryk Siemiradzki was born in what is now Ukraine to a Polish family and studied in Saint Petersburg, Munich and Rome. He lived mainly in Rome, where he painted giant, sunny pictures of ancient Greece and Rome. He was one of the most successful painters in Europe. He died in 1902.

Józef Chełmoński was born in a village in Poland and became one of the country's most beloved painters. He studied in Warsaw and Munich and lived in Paris for some years. He painted the Polish countryside, wide skies, horses and birds. He died in 1914.
Alfred Stevens was born in Brussels and settled in Paris, where he became a leading painter of elegant women in fashionable rooms. He was a friend of Manet and Degas. He died in Paris in 1906.

Fernand Khnopff was born in Belgium and became one of the leading Symbolist painters. He lived in Brussels and designed his own house. His quiet, mysterious pictures often show dreamlike women. He died in Brussels in 1921.

Gustaaf Wappers was born in Antwerp and became the leading Belgian Romantic history painter. He painted scenes of the Belgian Revolution of 1830. He lived in Brussels and Paris. He died in Paris in 1874.
Rik Wouters was a Belgian painter and sculptor born in 1882 in Mechelen. He painted his wife Nel in bright, happy colors. He died young, in Amsterdam, at 33, in 1916, after fleeing the war.

Théo van Rysselberghe was born in Ghent, Belgium, and was a leading painter in the pointillist style, which uses tiny dots of color. He painted portraits and summer landscapes. He spent his last years on the French Riviera. He died in 1926.

Arthur Streeton was born in Victoria, Australia, and became a leading painter of the Heidelberg School, a group of artists who painted outdoors. He is best known for golden, sunny landscapes. He later lived in London and returned to Australia. He died in 1943.

Charles Conder was born in England and raised in Australia. He became a member of the Heidelberg School at a young age. He later moved to Paris and London and painted silk fans and delicate landscapes. He died in London in 1909.

Frederick McCubbin was born in Melbourne and became a leading painter of the Heidelberg School. He painted the Australian bush and the pioneers with great feeling. He taught at the National Gallery school. He died in Melbourne in 1917.

George Washington Lambert was born in Saint Petersburg to American parents and moved to Australia as a child. He became a famous portrait painter and an official war artist at Gallipoli and in the Middle East. He died in 1930.

Tom Roberts was born in England and moved to Australia as a teenager. He was one of the leaders of the Heidelberg School, and he painted some of the most famous pictures of Australian life, including 'Shearing the Rams'. He died in 1931.
Benedito Calixto was a Brazilian painter born in 1853 in Itanhaém, near São Paulo. He painted history, religious subjects and the coast. He was also an historian. He died in São Paulo in 1927.

Pedro Américo was a Brazilian painter born in 1843 in Paraíba. He studied in Paris and painted huge history pictures, including 'Independence or Death!' He also wrote books and was a politician. He died in Florence, Italy, in 1905.

Victor Meirelles was born in Florianópolis, Brazil, and studied in Rio de Janeiro and Europe. He painted large pictures of the history of Brazil, such as 'The First Mass in Brazil'. He died in Rio de Janeiro in 1903.

Marquard Wocher was born in Germany in 1760 and settled in Basel, Switzerland. He is remembered for his huge circular painting of Thun and the Alps, one of the oldest panoramas in the world. He died in 1830.

Antonio Ciseri was born in Switzerland to Italian parents and worked in Florence. He painted religious subjects and portraits with great realism. His 'Ecce Homo' is his best-known work. He died in Florence in 1891.

Giovanni Segantini was born in Arco, in the Alps, and became a leading Italian painter of mountain scenes. He lived in the Swiss Alps, painting glowing, detailed landscapes and shepherds. He died at the age of 41 on a mountain peak, in 1899.

Carlos de Haes was born in Brussels and moved to Spain as a young man. He became the leading Spanish landscape painter, introducing a realistic, outdoor style. He taught at the Academy in Madrid. He died there in 1898.
